title: Integration tests: perform sensitive actions and assert audit events exist with required fields
creator: Nadia Rahman
description:
## Context
We’re standardizing audit logging around schema v1 and need confidence that “sensitive actions” actually result in persisted audit events with the required fields.

Unit tests + schema validation aren’t sufficient because:
- actor/request_id propagation can break across the gateway/service boundary
- events can be dropped/delayed in the pipeline (ingest/validate/store/export)
- the Console/API may emit different shapes unless we test through the real surfaces

This ticket adds end-to-end integration tests that:
1) perform selected sensitive actions through real APIs (and Console where needed)
2) poll the Audit Logs API until the corresponding event(s) appear
3) validate required fields + correlation semantics for schema v1

## Scope (initial set)
Target a small-but-representative set of actions across Hosted API + Console backend:
- API key create
- API key rotate
- API key revoke
- RBAC role create/update (at least one permission change)
- (optional if stable) model rollout action that is console-initiated (e.g., canary start/stop)

Out of scope for this ticket (covered by separate subsystem validation / later expansion):
- Dedicated scaling actions (Dedicated control plane test env constraints)
- Private installer upgrade/rollback (requires customer-like cluster harness)

## Approach
### Test runner + environment
- Use the existing staging E2E harness (runs against a dedicated staging org/workspace created for tests).
- Authenticate using a locked-down E2E admin service account (rotated by SRE) and create per-test temporary users/keys as needed.
- The tests should be safe to run repeatedly (idempotent cleanup; unique resource naming with run_id).

### Correlation strategy (avoid flakiness)
For each sensitive action request:
- capture request_id returned by gateway (or x-request-id echoed by client)
- query Audit Logs API with filters (org_id + request_id) and poll until found
- timeout defaults: 90s max wait, 2s initial backoff up to 10s

Rationale: audit pipeline is async; we should not assume immediate availability.

### Assertions
For each matched audit event:
- event_name matches the expected registry name(s) for the action
- event_version == "1" (schema v1)
- required envelope fields exist and are non-empty:
  - event_name
  - event_version
  - occurred_at
  - org_id (and workspace_id if applicable)
  - actor.* (type + id; email where available)
  - request_id
  - source_ip (when request originates from external surface)
  - user_agent (when request originates from external surface)
  - outcome (success/failure/denied) and error semantics when outcome != success
- target modeling:
  - target.type and target.id present for key/role resources
- redaction:
  - payload MUST NOT include raw secrets/tokens (assert common keys are absent: "api_key", "token", "secret", "authorization")

### Negative-path coverage (minimal)
Add one test that intentionally triggers an RBAC denial and asserts:
- an audit event exists with outcome == "denied"
- error.code is present (don’t overfit on exact string) and request_id correlates

## Implementation notes
- Tests should only depend on published schema/registry types from the shared audit logging package (ENG-2482) to avoid duplicating required-field lists.
- Do not parse internal pipeline DB directly; use the supported Audit Logs API (ENG-2493) to better match customer reality.
- Ensure tests emit debugging artifacts on failure:
  - the request_id
  - the Audit Logs API query used
  - the last N events returned for the org filtered by occurred_at window

## Rollout
- Phase 1: run nightly (non-blocking) to burn down flake and tune polling.
- Phase 2: make blocking for PRs that touch audit logging shared library, schema, or instrumentation (labels: audit-logging).

## Owners / reviewers
- Primary: Caleb Johnson (Tracing/metrics ingestion & correlation)
- Review: Kaitlyn Nguyen (Auth/RBAC & API keys), Chloe Martin (Console backend), Marcus Lin (Security Eng) for negative-path semantics

## Links
- PR implementing harness + initial tests: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18501
- Schema v1 definitions: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18421
- Registry enforcement: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18437
acceptance_criteria: E2E tests perform API key create/rotate/revoke and assert at least one schema-v1 audit event exists per action with request_id correlation.
E2E tests perform RBAC role create/update and assert a schema-v1 audit event exists with target modeling and required envelope fields.
At least one negative-path test asserts outcome == "denied" and includes error semantics without leaking secrets.
Tests validate required fields via shared schema/validator utilities (no duplicated ad-hoc required-field lists).
Tests are running in staging nightly with actionable failure logs (includes request_id + query details).
comments: 2025-06-07 (Caleb Johnson): Drafted approach to use Audit Logs API rather than pipeline DB access. Poll-by-request_id should keep us resilient to delivery lag; will default to 90s and tune based on SRE SLO numbers.

2025-06-11 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): For key rotation, there are two code paths (console vs API). Please make sure we exercise at least one console-backed route because that’s where actor propagation historically broke.

2025-06-14 (Chloe Martin): Audit Logs API filters support request_id + occurred_at window; pagination defaults to 100. Suggest we query by request_id first, then fall back to time-window if request_id is missing (but treat missing request_id as a test failure once gateway propagation is fully enforced).

2025-06-20 (Marcus Lin): On denied events: outcome should be "denied" not "failure"; error.code should be stable-ish (e.g., RBAC_DENIED) but don’t assert the exact message. Also add an assertion that payload redaction is enforced (no tokens).

2025-06-28 (Caleb Johnson): Implemented harness + API key/RBAC flows, added polling helper and debug dump on failure. Opened PR 18501. Running nightly first; we saw a few timeouts during exporter backlog—keeping 90s for now.

2025-07-08 (Nadia Rahman): Marking Done after merge + nightly job green for 5 consecutive runs. Follow-up: expand coverage to Dedicated + Private once their test environments are stable (track under ENG-2491/coverage expansion).
